findings.summary: The `human approval policy` check reports only `approval.substantial` and `approval.high_risk`, but the effective substantial gate also fires when an active profile declares `controls.human_approval in {True, "required"}` (runner.py:100-108). A user reading `approval.substantial=false` will conclude a substantial run executes end-to-end, and the tier line's hedge ("its effective human-approval gate") names a factor doctor never surfaces, so the two new lines together cannot answer the question they pose.
findings.evidence_required: Either (a) extend the policy detail to name profile-derived approval sources — e.g. append the active/declared profiles whose `controls.human_approval` is truthy, read from `config.profiles.definitions` — or (b) explicitly scope the detail as config-declared only (wording that says profiles may independently require approval), and add a test with a profile definition setting `human_approval: true` asserting the diagnostic does not imply an ungated substantial run.

findings.summary: No test covers a project.yaml with no `approval:` block at all — the shape of the existing `VALID_PROJECT_YAML` fixture and of the live `.ai/project.yaml` before it was populated. The planned tests only use explicit values, so nothing pins that the check still appears and renders the `ApprovalPolicy` defaults.
findings.evidence_required: A test using a config without an `approval:` key asserting `human approval policy` is present with detail exactly `approval.substantial=false; approval.high_risk=true` (the model defaults at config/models.py:92-93).

findings.summary: The plan requires a test that monkeypatches the doctor module's registry view, but never states that the supported/unsupported split must be computed inside `run_checks` at call time. A module-level precomputation from `TIER_STAGES` at import satisfies every other instruction and makes the prescribed monkeypatch test unable to observe the change.
findings.evidence_required: Plan text stating the sets are derived inside the check function on each `run_checks` call (no import-time constant), so `monkeypatch.setattr(doctor_module, "TIER_STAGES", ...)` is observable.

findings.summary: `render()` emits only `✓`/`!`, so the tier check renders as a passing line whose limitation text sits at the tail of a ~330-character detail. The docstring amendment documents the semantics but does not make the limitation legible to someone scanning doctor output for `!` markers.
findings.evidence_required: Either a rationale for keeping the current ordering, or a detail string that leads with the unsupported/gated facts before the `registry-supported=` enumeration, with the render-level test asserting that ordering.
